rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both proclamations establish a national monument under the Antiquities Act using the same linked machinery: reserve federally owned or controlled lands within specified boundaries, withdraw them from appropriation under the public-land laws, automatically reserve nonfederal inholdings upon federal acquisition of title, preserve valid existing rights, and warn against unauthorized damage or settlement. C13 and C11 also contain meaningful components of this pattern, especially contingent incorporation of nonfederal lands; C13 additionally parallels the child's dominant-reservation clause. But C04 is the strongest overall match because it combines the establishment function with the federal-land withdrawal and future-acquisition provisions in nearly the same operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: there are hereby set apart and reserved as the Aniakchak National Monument all lands, including submerged lands, and waters owned or controlled by the United States within the boundaries
shared_material.parent_excerpt: federally owned or controlled lands within the exterior boundaries of the following described area are hereby reserved from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws and set apart as the Marble Canyon National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both use a combined reservation, public-land withdrawal, and monument-establishment clause directed at federally owned or controlled lands within defined boundaries.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Lands, including submerged lands, and waters within these boundaries not owned by the United States shall be reserved as a part of the monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: State-owned lands within those boundaries shall become and be reserved as parts of that monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.explanation: This is substantially the same contingent-incorporation mechanism, adapted from state-owned lands to all nonfederal lands and waters.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The establishment of this monument is subject to valid existing rights
shared_material.explanation: The same savings condition accompanies the operative reservation, although this clause alone would be routine.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Nothing in this Proclamation shall be deemed to revoke any existing withdrawal, reservation or appropriation ... however, the national monument shall be the dominant reservation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The reservation made by this proclamation is not intended to prevent the use of the lands ... for national-forest purposes ... but the reservation for the national-monument purposes shall be the dominant reservation
shared_material.explanation: C13, the second-ranked alternative, supplies especially distinctive language for preserving overlapping withdrawals while making the monument reservation dominant.
